title: Linear and logistic regression from scratch

wrong.ols_no_intercept.py: normal_equation fits the intercept column but returns b = 0, so any data with an offset is fit badly
wrong.ridge_penalises_intercept.py: ridge_fit shrinks the intercept too, so shifting every label no longer shifts only b
wrong.ridge_penalty_is_sqrt_lambda.py: ridge_fit uses sqrt(lam) as the penalty strength, so it matches the closed form only at lam = 0 or 1
wrong.sigmoid_overflows.py: sigmoid computes 1/(1+exp(-z)) directly, which overflows for large negative z
wrong.loss_takes_log_of_probability.py: logistic_loss takes log(p) of a saturated probability, giving inf or nan for confident-and-wrong logits
wrong.grad_sums_instead_of_mean.py: logistic_grad sums over the batch instead of averaging, so the gradient is n times too big and fails the finite-difference check
wrong.grad_has_wrong_sign.py: logistic_grad returns y - p instead of p - y, so descent climbs the loss
wrong.gd_never_updates_bias.py: logistic_gd updates only the weights, so the decision boundary is stuck through the origin

hints: Add a column of ones to X so the intercept is just another weight. The normal equations are (A^T A) theta = A^T y; solve them with np.linalg.solve. For ridge add lam on the diagonal, but leave the intercept's diagonal entry at 0.

A stable sigmoid uses exp(-|z|): for z >= 0 it is 1/(1+e), for z < 0 it is e/(1+e) with e = exp(-|z|). The cross-entropy -[y log s + (1-y) log(1-s)] equals log(1+e^z) - y z, which np.logaddexp(0, z) computes without overflow.
The gradient of mean cross-entropy is simple: with r = sigmoid(Xw + b) - y, grad_w = X^T r / n and grad_b = mean(r). Gradient descent starts at zero and repeats w -= lr * grad_w, b -= lr * grad_b.
